scope: plain-language draft (lead, blocks, annotations, readdown, worth-checking, hypothesis revisions) and the claims they cite

overall.summary: All 78 claims and every number in the draft reproduce, and probes confirm the thresholds, counts and directions. Two wording problems: the sex-by-exercise-angina sentence says the drop is bigger without exercise angina, which holds on the log-odds scale but not in the percentages it quotes, and 'biggest first' in the linear block does not match the order given. Three domain flags (fixed defect, high fasting sugar, thallium code 4) are correctly raised as worth-checking.

findings.statement: Being a woman rather than a man lowers the predicted risk, and even more so if exercise does not bring on chest pain: from about 20% to below 1% without chest pain on exercise, and from about 27% to about 1% with it.
findings.evidence: Risks 19.7% -> 0.2% (no exercise angina) and 27.4% -> 1.0% (exercise angina). On the log-odds scale the drop is larger without exercise angina (4.89 vs 3.65), as C45 says ('amplified'). In the percentages the sentence itself quotes, the drop is smaller without exercise angina (19.5 vs 26.4 points; C45 delta -0.0696). A reader will read 'even more so' against the percentages. Same text in blocks[2] and annotations.ann_32[0].

findings.statement: These inputs add up independently, biggest first: ...
findings.check: claim effect sizes (log-odds) against the order of the block's sentences
findings.evidence: Order given: vessels 4.63, flat ST 3.60, cholesterol 2.57, blood pressure 1.53, then typical angina -4.43, non-anginal -3.39, woman -3.65. Typical angina and being a woman are larger than flat ST, cholesterol and blood pressure but come last, and the last three are not in size order. 'Biggest first' holds only within the raising inputs. Same text in blocks[0] and annotations.ann_36.

findings.statement: the model treats a fixed thallium defect as lowering the predicted risk (20% -> 1%, n = 15)
findings.evidence: the sentence is accurate about the model; the observed rate among fixed-defect patients is 60% vs 43% in the rest, so the data do not support a protective effect either. Correctly flagged.
